ops.title: spawnllm config isolation: flag-only design rationale
ops.body:
# spawnllm — flag-only config isolation per backend

## Why

spawnllm spawns provider CLIs (`claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `agy`), which inherited the host's ambient config (settings layers, MCP servers, hooks) — non-reproducible, leaks behavior/cost. Goal: isolate config on every spawned run, behind a `RunSpec.isolated` toggle (default `True`) that the high-level helpers always use.

## The key result: isolation is FLAG-only

Verification overturned two assumptions. **A backend can be isolated only if it has an isolation *flag* that doesn't touch auth; relocating a config home always strands auth.**

1. **A fresh `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` logs Claude out** (`Not logged in · Please run /login`). The keychain token (`Claude Code-credentials`) exists, but the logged-in linkage (`oauthAccount`) lives in `~/.claude.json`, absent from a relocated dir. So the "fresh dir" idea is unusable — use flags only.
2. **Gemini's only relocation lever `GEMINI_CLI_HOME` strips its OAuth auth-method** (`set an Auth method`). Same class as `agy`, which has no config-home override and entangles onboarding state with its config dir (a `HOME` override makes it prompt to auth).

| Backend | Isolation (when `spec.isolated`) | Auth preserved by |
|---|---|---|
| Claude | flags `--setting-sources ""` **+** `--strict-mcp-config` (hoisted after `--model`) | keychain OAuth, untouched |
| Codex | flag `--ignore-user-config` (skips `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml`; "auth still uses CODEX_HOME") | `auth.json` in the real `CODEX_HOME` (never relocate it — single-use refresh tokens, openai/codex#15410) |
| Gemini | none — no isolation flag; relocation strips OAuth | reads real config (no-flag exception) |
| agy | none — no config-home override; onboarding entangled | reads real config (no-flag exception) |

## What was implemented

- `spawnllm/spec.py`: `RunSpec.isolated: bool = True`. Helpers build the spec with the default; `run`/`run_sync` callers can pass `isolated=False` for ambient config.
- `backends/claude.py` `build_command`: after `--model`, `*(["--setting-sources",""] if spec.isolated else [])` then `*(["--strict-mcp-config"] if spec.isolated or cfg.strict_mcp else [])`; dropped `--strict-mcp-config` from the explicit branch and the default branch (now just `["--system-prompt",""]`).
- `backends/codex.py` `command_for`: `*(["--ignore-user-config"] if spec.isolated else [])` after `--model`.
- `env()` stays zero-arg returning `{}` on every backend. (An interim env-relocation approach — a new `isolation.py`, an `env(self, spec)` signature, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`/`GEMINI_CLI_HOME` overrides, cred symlinking — was built then fully reverted once flags proved sufficient and relocation proved auth-breaking. Don't reintroduce it.)
- `tests/test_backends.py`: Claude argv carries `--setting-sources "" --strict-mcp-config`; `isolated=False` drops both; Codex carries `--ignore-user-config`; Gemini/agy assert `env() == {}`.
- `cc-context/bench`: no signature change (env stayed zero-arg). Its `claude -p` runs inherit the isolation flags via `backend.invocation(spec)`; `arms.py` header comment updated.

## Verified

`uv run --no-sync pytest` (spawnllm + bench) green; `ty check` clean. Real smoke: `call_sync('Reply with exactly: ok')` → `ok`; init envelope `mcp_servers: []`, `apiKeySource: none` — isolated AND authenticated. agy works un-isolated.

## Open

- Codex small-tier `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` exits 1 in this env (isolated and not) — unrelated to isolation.
- Gemini isolation is unverified (this account's Code Assist tier is retired). With a working OAuth account or `GEMINI_API_KEY`, a "relocate + require API key" path could revisit it.
ops.when: Before modifying spawnllm backend isolation, config flags, or revisiting the config-relocation vs flags trade-off
